content:
# Git-bus shared ledger — design

**Model:** one bare repo is the bus; `main` is the only branch. Sovereignty = path ownership: each writer may *only append* inside its own directory. Read is universal; write is exclusive. You own your outbox; your inbox is everyone else's outbox. The watcher owns one reply stream per agent.

## 1. File layout

```
bus.git/                               # bare upstream — the bus
└── hooks/pre-receive                  # enforces ownership, append-only, chain, signatures

agent clone/
├── .bus/
│   ├── policy.json                    # ownership map + rate limits (§3)
│   ├── schema/entry-v1.json           # JSON Schema for ledger lines
│   └── keys/{alpha,beta,watcher}.pub  # pinned ed25519 pubkeys
├── ledger/
│   ├── alpha/2025-06-01.jsonl         # alpha-only appends (UTC-day partitions)
│   ├── beta/2025-06-01.jsonl          # beta-only appends
│   └── watcher/
│       ├── to-alpha/2025-06-01.jsonl  # watcher's replies addressed to alpha
│       └── to-beta/2025-06-01.jsonl   # watcher's replies addressed to beta
├── blobs/<writer>/<sha256>            # oversized payloads, content-addressed, writer-owned
└── state/                             # read pointers — caches only; each writer owns its own
    ├── alpha/ack.json
    ├── beta/ack.json
    └── watcher/cursor.json
```

- All writes are disjoint by directory → `pull --rebase` never conflicts; the only contention is a push race, resolved by rebase + retry.
- Partitions rotate at UTC midnight or 8 MiB, whichever first. Full history lives in git itself (`git show <rev>:ledger/...`); the working tree only needs today + yesterday.

## 2. Provenance stamp

One JSON entry per line; the stamp is **in-band** so it survives rebases and cherry-picks (commit metadata is secondary).

```json
{"v":1,"id":"01JZQ8Z3M5K7R9T2W4Y6Z8A0B","ts":"2025-06-01T12:34:56.789Z",
 "writer":"alpha","seq":4127,"prev":"9f1c02aa77e1...","type":"observation",
 "ref":null,"body":{...},"sig":"ed25519:MEUCIQ..."}
```

- `seq` — per-writer, strictly +1, no gaps (hook-enforced). Ordering truth is `(writer, seq)`; `ts` is advisory (clocks skew).
- `prev` — SHA-256 of the writer's previous canonical entry → a per-writer hash chain that spans partitions (first line of a new day links to the last line of the prior day). Genesis `prev` = anchor pinned in `policy.json`. Any insert/delete/rewrite breaks the chain, so **append-only is verifiable, not just promised**.
- `ref` — for replies: `{"writer":"beta","seq":918,"id":"...","digest":"..."}` (or a `from_seq/to_seq` range for digest replies).
- `sig` — ed25519 over the canonical form: sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, `sig` field excluded.

Canonical one-line stamp for logs and summaries:

```
alpha#4127@01JZQ8Z3M5K7R9T2W4Y6Z8A0B sha256=9f1c02aa77e1 2025-06-01T12:34:56.789Z observation
beta#918@01JZQ8Z...                  sha256=c44e19bb02af 2025-06-01T12:36:01.102Z reply→alpha#4127
```

## 3. Rate limits

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "ownership": {
    "alpha":   ["ledger/alpha/**", "state/alpha/**", "blobs/alpha/**"],
    "beta":    ["ledger/beta/**",  "state/beta/**",  "blobs/beta/**"],
    "watcher": ["ledger/watcher/**","state/watcher/**","blobs/watcher/**"]
  },
  "limits": {
    "entry_max_bytes": 65536,
    "body_max_bytes": 32768,
    "commits_per_hour_per_writer": 120,
    "min_commit_interval_s": 30,
    "max_entries_per_commit": 50,
    "alert_bypass_per_hour": 5,
    "push_backoff_s": [1, 2, 4, 8, 16],
    "push_max_attempts": 5
  },
  "watcher": {
    "cadence_s": 300,
    "max_replies_per_cycle_per_agent": 40,
    "max_backlog_per_agent": 200,
    "stale_after_silence_s": 900
  },
  "heartbeat_cadence_s": 300
}
```

Rationale: 120 commits/h/writer ≈ one git op per 30 s, amortized by batching up to 50 lines per commit. `type:"alert"` skips the debounce but is capped at 5/h so it can't become the main channel. Entries >64 KiB go to `blobs/` with the digest in the line. Backlog >200 per agent → the watcher emits one `digest` entry covering the range instead of per-entry replies (backpressure).

## 4. Enforcement — how "never edit each other's" is real

`pre-receive` hook on the bus, per push:

1. Map pushing identity → owned globs; **reject any changed path outside them**.
2. For each modified ledger file: new blob must have the old blob as a byte prefix (pure append).
3. Recompute the writer's chain over touched partitions; verify `prev` linkage and `seq` continuity.
4. Verify `sig` against the pinned pubkey.

Client discipline: one writer process per agent (file lock around seq allocation + append); on restart, verify chain against HEAD and truncate any uncommitted tail line. `policy.json` and keys change only via signed maintainer commits.

## 5. Watcher loop

```
every 300 s:
  git pull --rebase
  for agent in {alpha, beta}:
      since = max ref.seq in my to-<agent>/ log        # replies ARE the durable cursor
      new   = ledger/<agent>/*.jsonl lines after since
      batch = new[:40]   (or one digest reply if |new| > 200)
      append chained+signed replies, ref = source stamp → ledger/watcher/to-<agent>/<today>.jsonl
      one commit: "watcher: alpha#4128..4141 beta#918..930"
  git pull --rebase && git push                        # backoff 1,2,4,8,16 s, 5 tries
```

Crash-safety: because every reply carries `ref`, the watcher's own reply log is the authoritative cursor — on recovery, scan it for the max `ref.seq` (or `to_seq` for digests) per agent and resume; no double-replies, `state/watcher/cursor.json` is a pure cache. Writers heartbeat every 300 s even when idle; the watcher flags silence > 900 s as stale. Agents consume replies by reading their `to-<agent>/` stream; direct agent-to-agent replies work the same way — write to your own log with `ref` pointing at the other's stamp.
reasoning:
The user is asking me to design a shared ledger over a "git bus" — a communication/coordination architecture where two sovereign agents each append to their own files (never editing each other's files), and a watcher agent auto-replies on a cadence. They want:

1. File layout
2. Provenance stamp format
3. Rate limits

This is a design/engineering question. Let me actually think hard about this and produce a concrete, well-engineered answer.

Key concepts:
- "Git bus" — using a git repository as a message bus / coordination medium. Commits are messages. Branches or directories are channels. This is a real pattern (git-as-database, git-as-message-bus).
- Two sovereign agents: Agent A and Agent B. Sovereign = they have full authority over their own files, no cross-writes. Append-only to own files.
- Watcher: a third process (or one of them, or an automation like a CI bot) that watches the bus and auto-replies on cadence (e.g., every N seconds/minutes, it reads new entries and posts replies into its own file or into a replies directory).
- Never edit each other's files: append-only discipline, enforced by conventions + optionally by CI checks / pre-receive hooks.

Design decisions to make:

**Repository structure.** Options:
- One file per agent (append-only JSONL or NDJSON log): `ledger/agent-alpha.log`, `ledger/agent-beta.log`.
- Or one file per agent per day/partition: `ledger/agent-alpha/2025-01-01.jsonl` to bound file size and merge conflicts.
- Watcher replies: watcher appends to its own file(s), e.g., `ledger/watcher/...` or `replies/agent-alpha.jsonl`? But "never edit each other's" — replies should go into the watcher's own files, with references (correlation IDs) back to the entries being replied to. Alternatively a `replies/` tree owned by the watcher.

Actually, let me think about the topology. Two sovereign agents A and B, plus a watcher W. The watcher auto-replies on cadence. So likely:
- A appends to A's log.
- B appends to B's log.
- W watches both, and appends replies. Where do W's replies live? Options:
  a. W's own log: `ledger/watcher.jsonl`, entries reference (agent, seq, digest) of the entry being answered.
  b. Per-target reply streams owned by W: `replies/to-alpha.jsonl`, `replies/to-beta.jsonl`. Still owned by W; A and B never write there. This makes consumption easy: each agent reads its inbox.

I like (b) with a top-level inbox concept: each agent has an `outbox` (their own append log) and an `inbox` (written by others, read-only for them). But the constraint "never edit each other's files" — if B writes into A's inbox, B is editing A's file? No — appending to A's inbox file would be a cross-write. To keep strict sovereignty, the writer must own the file. So inboxes should be owned by the sender: `outboxes/alpha.jsonl` (A writes), `outboxes/beta.jsonl` (B writes), `outboxes/watcher/...` (W writes). Readers read others' outboxes. That's the clean mailbox inversion: you own your outbox; inboxes are just other people's outboxes you subscribe to. This is exactly how git-based buses and mail spools work (like NNTP/Usenet or maildir with ownership).

So layout:

```
bus/                                  (git repo, bare upstream + working clones)
├── .bus/
│   ├── policy.json                   (rate limits, schema version, cadence)
│   └── schema/entry.schema.json      (JSON Schema for ledger entries)
├── ledger/
│   ├── alpha/
│   │   ├── 2025-06-01.jsonl          (agent alpha's append-only log, partitioned by day)
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── beta/
│   │   └── 2025-06-01.jsonl
│   └── watcher/
│       ├── replies-to-alpha/2025-06-01.jsonl
│       └── replies-to-beta/2025-06-01.jsonl
├── state/                            (optional high-water marks / checkpoints, each owned)
│   ├── alpha/ack.json                (alpha's read pointer over beta + watcher)
│   ├── beta/ack.json
│   └── watcher/cursor.json           (watcher's read pointers over alpha & beta)
└── README.md / POLICY.md
```

Hmm, but partitioning by day creates many files; alternative: single file per agent with rotation at N MB. Day partitioning is simpler and plays nicely with git diffs. Let me offer day partitioning with a rotation rule.

Actually, maybe simpler: single append-only file per stream, rotated when > 8 MB or at UTC midnight, whichever first. Keep it concrete.

**Branching strategy.** Should agents work on separate branches and merge? That adds merge machinery. Simpler: all on one branch (`main`), since each agent writes only its own directory, so no textual conflicts. Git handles concurrent appends to different files fine. But two agents committing simultaneously → push races; one push gets rejected, must pull --rebase and retry. That's the standard optimistic concurrency. Alternatively, per-agent branches (`agent/alpha`, `agent/beta`, `watcher/main`) merged by the watcher — but that reintroduces a merge bottleneck and the watcher would be editing the main branch. The single-branch, disjoint-directories design is cleanest: conflicts are structurally impossible at file level; only push races occur, resolved by rebase (which for disjoint files never conflicts).

Wait — one subtlety: if two agents append to the same file (their own file) from two processes, that's their own problem; each agent should serialize its own writes with a lock. Note that.

**Commit discipline.** Each append = one commit (or batched appends = one commit containing multiple lines, but then per-line provenance must be inside the entry, not just the commit). Better: provenance stamp lives inside each JSONL line so it survives rebase/cherry-pick, and the commit carries complementary metadata (author, timestamp, signature). The entry should include:
- `v`: schema version
- `id`: entry ID (ULID for sortability)
- `ts`: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp with milliseconds
- `agent`: writer identity (matches git author + directory)
- `seq`: monotonic per-writer sequence number (gap detection)
- `prev`: digest of writer's previous entry (hash chain → tamper-evidence, append-only enforcement)
- `type`: message type (e.g., `claim`, `observation`, `reply`, `heartbeat`)
- `ref`: optional correlation — (agent, seq/id, digest) of entry being replied to
- `body`: payload
- `sig`: signature over the canonical entry (minus sig field) — optional but recommended for sovereignty (agent's key signs its own entries)

Hash chain per writer: `prev = sha256(canonical(prev_entry))`. Genesis entry has `prev = null` and maybe a `genesis` anchor in policy. Chain gives: (a) proof nothing was inserted/removed/reordered, (b) enforcement of append-only (a rewritten file breaks the chain at the rewrite point).

**Provenance stamp.** The user explicitly asks for "the provenance stamp." Give a concrete format. Something like:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "01J2XQ8Z3M5K7R9T2W4Y6Z8A0B",
  "ts": "2025-06-01T12:34:56.789Z",
  "writer": "alpha",
  "seq": 4127,
  "prev": "b3f2c9…64",
  "body": { ... },
  "sig": "ed25519:BASE64SIG"
}
```

And the canonicalization rule: JSON with sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8, sig field excluded, digest = SHA-256 of canonical bytes. Also a one-line "provenance stamp" string form for logs/summaries:

`alpha#4127@01J2XQ8Z3M5K7R9T2W4Y6Z8A0B:sha256=9f1c…e2:2025-06-01T12:34:56.789Z`

Something like `<writer>#<seq>@<ulid>:<digest-prefix>:<ts>`. Good.

Also the git-side provenance: commit author/committer, and ideally a `Signed-off-by` or commit signature. The entry-level stamp is the durable one because rebases rewrite commits but not file contents.

**Watcher cadence.** The watcher runs on a schedule (cron / systemd timer / CI schedule). Cadence options: every 60s poll; or event-driven via `git receive-pack` hook + cadence floor. The user says "auto-replies on cadence," so: watcher wakes every T (e.g., 5 min), fetches, reads new entries since cursor, generates one reply per entry (or a batched digest reply), appends to `ledger/watcher/replies-to-<agent>/…`, commits, pushes. Rate limits apply to watcher too (max replies per cycle per agent, min interval).

**Rate limits.** Concrete numbers:
- Per-writer append rate: max 1 commit per 10s per writer? Or token bucket: burst 10, refill 1/min? Let's think about what's sane for a git bus. Git operations aren't free; a busy bus could do hundreds of commits/day easily. Sane defaults:
  - Max appends per writer per rolling hour: e.g., 120 (avg one per 30s).
  - Max entries per commit: 50 (batching encouraged); min commit interval per writer: 30s (debounce), except `type=alert` bypass with separate budget.
  - Max entry size: 64 KiB; max body size 32 KiB; oversized payloads go to `blobs/<sha256>` and entry references the blob.
  - Watcher cadence: every 300s (5 min); max 1 reply per inbound entry, max 40 replies per cycle per agent; replies must be batched into one commit per cycle per target.
  - Global repo guards: max repo growth per day (e.g., 200 MB), retention: compact/rotate files > 8 MB into monthly archives, keep full history in `archive/` or rely on git history itself (git already keeps history — rotation is for working-tree ergonomics, and old data is addressable via git history).
  - Push retries: exponential backoff 1s→2s→4s→…→max 60s, jitter, max 5 attempts, then park in local spool.
  - Alert/priority lane: `type: "alert"` entries bypass the 30s debounce but capped at 5/hour/writer.

**Enforcement.** How to guarantee "never edit each other's files" and append-only:
- Path ownership map in `.bus/policy.json`: `alpha` → `ledger/alpha/**`, `state/alpha/**`; `beta` → `ledger/beta/**`, `state/beta/**`; `watcher` → `ledger/watcher/**`, `state/watcher/**`, plus policy/schema files (or a separate `maintainer` role).
- Pre-receive hook on the bare repo (or CI check): for each ref update, diff old→new; every changed path must be under the pushing writer's prefix; every modification to an existing ledger file must be append-only: verify that the new file's first N bytes equal the old file (prefix property) — i.e., new blob starts with old blob's content. Implement via `git diff --raw` and for each modified file, `git cat-file` old blob and check new blob starts with it (or hash-chain validation covers it).
- Chain validation: CI/hook recomputes each writer's chain over the changed partition; a non-append edit breaks `prev` linkage → reject.
- Signatures: hook verifies ed25519 sig against per-writer pubkey pinned in `.bus/keys/alpha.pub` etc. Key rotation via signed policy commits by a maintainer quorum.

Also mention: agents must `git pull --rebase` before push; because writes are disjoint, rebase never conflicts; push race is the only contention.

**Watcher reply semantics.** Reply entry includes `ref: {"agent":"alpha","id":"<ulid>","digest":"…"}` and `body: {…}`. Watcher cursor in `state/watcher/cursor.json`: `{ "alpha": {"partition":"2025-06-01","seq":4127}, "beta": {...} }`. Cursor updates are commits owned by watcher. Idempotency: watcher must not reply twice to same entry — cursor + reply index; on crash between commit-of-replies and commit-of-cursor, recover by scanning own replies for max `ref.seq` per agent (replies themselves are the durable cursor — nice property: derive cursor from last reply, cursor file is just an optimization). Actually simpler: make cursor derived: `next_seq = last_replied_seq + 1`, computed by scanning watcher's own reply log. Keep cursor file as cache. Good design point to mention.

**Heartbeats/liveness.** Writers emit `type:"heartbeat"` on cadence (e.g., every 5 min) even if idle; watcher flags silence > 3× cadence as stale. Maybe optional; include briefly.

**Clock discipline.** Timestamps from writer clocks can skew; ULID gives ordering; per-writer `seq` is the truth for ordering; `ts` is advisory. Note monotonicity requirement: `seq` must be strictly +1; hook rejects gaps/dupes.

**File layout final:**

```
bus.git/                        # bare upstream (the bus)
  ├── hooks/pre-receive         # ownership + append-only + chain + sig checks
  └── ...

working clone/
├── .bus/
│   ├── policy.json
│   ├── schema/entry-v1.schema.json
│   └── keys/{alpha,beta,watcher}.pub
├── ledger/
│   ├── alpha/2025-06-01.jsonl          # alpha-owned append-only
│   ├── beta/2025-06-01.jsonl           # beta-owned append-only
│   └── watcher/
│       ├── to-alpha/2025-06-01.jsonl   # watcher-owned replies to alpha
│       └── to-beta/2025-06-01.jsonl    # watcher-owned replies to beta
├── blobs/                              # content-addressed large payloads (writer-owned subdirs? or shared)
└── state/
    ├── alpha/ack.json                  # alpha-owned read pointers (cache)
    ├── beta/ack.json
    └── watcher/cursor.json             # watcher-owned
```

blobs: to preserve sovereignty, `blobs/<writer>/<sha256>` — writer-owned. Fine.

```json

  "version": 1,
  "ownership": {
    "alpha":   ["ledger/alpha/**", "state/alpha/**", "blobs/alpha/**"],
    "beta":    ["ledger/beta/**", "state/beta/**", "blobs/beta/**"],
    "watcher": ["ledger/watcher/**", "state/watcher/**", "blobs/watcher/**"]
  },
  "limits": {
    "entry_max_bytes": 65536,
    "body_max_bytes": 32768,
    "commits_per_hour_per_writer": 120,

  },

  },

```

**Entry schema concrete:**

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "id": "01JZQ8Z3M5K7R9T2W4Y6Z8A0B",
  "ts": "2025-06-01T12:34:56.789Z",
  "writer": "alpha",
  "seq": 4127,
  "prev": "9f1c…e2",
  "type": "observation",
  "ref": null,
  "body": {"...": "..."},
  "sig": "ed25519:MEUCIQ…"
}
```

Canonical form: sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, exclude `sig`. digest = sha256 hex. `prev` of first entry of a partition = digest of last entry of previous partition (chain spans partitions — important detail so rotation doesn't reset the chain). Genesis `prev` = `"genesis"` or the chain anchor published in policy at onboarding.

**Provenance stamp (string form):**

`<writer>#<seq>@<ulid> sha256=<first12> <ts> <type>[ -> <ref-writer>#<ref-seq>]`

Example:
`alpha#4127@01JZQ8Z3M5K7R9T2W4Y6Z8A0B sha256=9f1c02aa77e1 2025-06-01T12:34:56.789Z observation`

And reply stamp includes `→beta#918`.

Also mention the dual stamp: entry stamp (in-band, survives rebase) + git commit stamp (out-of-band: commit sha, author, committer time, push cert). The entry stamp is canonical.

**Watcher loop pseudocode** — give it briefly:

```
every 300s:
  git pull --rebase
  for agent in [alpha, beta]:
    new = entries(agent, since=last_replied_seq(agent))
    replies = [reply(r) for r in new][:40]
    append replies → ledger/watcher/to-<agent>/<today>.jsonl (chained, signed)
    single commit "watcher: reply batch alpha#4128..4131, beta#918..920"
  git pull --rebase && git push (with backoff)
```

**Agent append pseudocode:**

```
lock(own spool)
entry = {…, seq: last_seq+1, prev: last_digest}
validate locally (schema, chain)
append line to today's partition
commit (debounced, batched ≤50)
pull --rebase; push with backoff
```

**Edge cases to mention:**
- Push race: rebase; disjoint dirs → no textual conflicts; chain intact because file content unchanged by rebase.
- Two processes of same writer: local file lock + seq allocation under lock.
- Crash between append and commit: uncommitted line is orphan; on restart, truncate to last committed line (verify chain against HEAD).
- Watcher crash between reply commit and cursor update: derive cursor from own replies (durable), cursor file is cache only.
- Rotation: chain spans partitions via prev linking; readers walk partitions in order.
- Repo growth: git history is the archive; working tree holds current day + yesterday; older via `git show <rev>:ledger/...`.
- Time skew: ordering by (writer, seq), not ts; ts advisory; ULID embeds ms timestamp for global sortability.

# Git-bus ledger: design

**Model:** one bare repo is the bus; `main` is the only branch. Sovereignty = path ownership: each agent exclusively owns its directory and may only append. Readers subscribe to others' files. You own your outbox; your inbox is everyone else's outbox. Watcher owns reply streams, one per agent.

## 1. File layout

```
bus.git/                              # bare upstream — the bus
└── hooks/pre-receive                 # enforces ownership, append-only, chain, signatures

agent clone/
├── .bus/
│   ├── policy.json                   # ownership map + limits (below)
│   ├── schema/entry-v1.json          # JSON Schema for ledger lines
│   └── keys/{alpha,beta,watcher}.pub # pinned ed25519 pubkeys
├── ledger/
│   ├── alpha/2025-06-01.jsonl        # alpha-only appends (UTC-day partitions)
│   ├── beta/2025-06-01.jsonl         # beta-only appends
│   └── watcher/
│       ├── to-alpha/2025-06-01.jsonl # watcher's replies addressed to alpha
│       └── to-beta/2025-06-01.jsonl  # watcher's replies addressed to beta
├── blobs/<writer>/<sha256>           # oversized payloads, content-addressed, writer-owned
└── state/                            # read pointers — caches only, each writer owns its own
    ├── alpha/ack.json
    ├── beta/ack.json
    └── watcher/cursor.json
```

Rules: single branch `main`; all writes disjoint by directory → rebase never conflicts; only contention is push race → `pull --rebase` + retry. Partition rotation at UTC midnight or 8 MiB, whichever first; history lives in git itself (`git show <rev>:ledger/...`).

## 2. Provenance stamp

Every line is one JSON entry; the stamp is in-band so it survives rebases and cherry-picks (commit metadata is secondary).

```json
{"v":1,"id":"01JZQ8Z3M5K7R9T2W4Y6Z8A0B","ts":"2025-06-01T12:34:56.789Z",
 "writer":"alpha","seq":4127,"prev":"9f1c02aa77e1…","type":"observation",
 "ref":null,"body":{...},"sig":"ed25519:MEUCIQ…"}
```

- `seq` — per-writer, strictly +1, no gaps (hook-enforced). Ordering truth = (writer, seq); `ts` advisory.
- `prev` — SHA-256 of the writer's previous canonical entry → per-writer hash chain spanning partitions (first line of a new partition links to last line of previous). Genesis `prev` = anchor published in `.bus/policy.json`. Any rewrite/insert/delete breaks the chain → append-only is verifiable, not just promised.
- `ref` — for replies: `{"writer":"beta","seq":918,"id":"…","digest":"…"}`.
- `sig` — ed25519 over the canonical form: sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, `sig` excluded.

Canonical one-line stamp for logs/summaries:

```
alpha#4127@01JZQ8Z3M5K7R9T2W4Y6Z8A0B sha256=9f1c02aa77e1 2025-06-01T12:34:56.789Z observation
beta#918@… sha256=… … reply→alpha#4127
```

## 3. Rate limits

policy.json:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "ownership": {
    "alpha":   ["ledger/alpha/**", "state/alpha/**", "blobs/alpha/**"],
    "beta":    ["ledger/beta/**",  "state/beta/**",  "blobs/beta/**"],
    "watcher": ["ledger/watcher/**","state/watcher/**","blobs/watcher/**"]
  },
  "limits": {
    "entry_max_bytes": 65536,
    "body_max_bytes": 32768,
    "commits_per_hour_per_writer": 120,
    "min_commit_interval_s": 30,
    "max_entries_per_commit": 50,
    "alert_bypass_per_hour": 5,
    "push_backoff_s": [1, 2, 4, 8, 16],
    "push_max_attempts": 5
  },
  "watcher": {
    "cadence_s": 300,
    "max_replies_per_cycle_per_agent": 40,
    "max_backlog_per_agent": 200,
    "stale_after_silence_s": 900
  },
  "heartbeat_cadence_s": 300
}
```

Notes on the numbers:
- 120 commits/h/writer ≈ one per 30 s; batch up to 50 lines per commit to amortize git ops.
- `type:"alert"` skips the 30 s debounce, capped 5/h/writer so it can't become the main channel.
- Watcher: wakes every 300 s, replies 1:1 to each new entry, max 40/cycle/agent; backlog >200 → emit a `digest` entry summarizing the overflow instead of per-entry replies (backpressure).
- Writers heartbeat every 300 s even when idle; watcher marks an agent stale after 900 s silence.
- Entry >64 KiB: write body to `blobs/<writer>/<sha256>`, entry carries the digest.

## 4. Enforcement (how "never edit each other's" is real)

pre-receive hook on the bus, per push:
1. Map pushing identity → owned globs; reject any changed path outside them.
2. For each modified ledger file: new blob must have the old blob as a byte prefix (pure append).
3. Recompute the writer's chain over touched partitions; verify `prev` links and `seq` continuity.
4. Verify `sig` against the pinned pubkey.

Plus client discipline: one writer process per agent (file lock around seq allocation + append); on restart, truncate any uncommitted tail line after verifying chain against HEAD.

## 5. Watcher loop

```
every 300 s:
  git pull --rebase
  for agent in {alpha, beta}:
      since = last ref.seq in my to-<agent>/ log (durable cursor; state/watcher/cursor.json is a cache)
      new   = ledger/<agent>/* since since
      batch = new[:40]  (or digest-entry if len(new) > 200)
      append chained+signed replies with ref=<entry stamp> → to-<agent>/<today>.jsonl
      one commit: "watcher: alpha#4128..4141 beta#918..930"
  git pull --rebase && git push   # backoff 1,2,4,8,16 s
```

Crash-safety: replies are the durable cursor — on recovery, scan own reply log for the max `ref.seq` per agent and resume from there; no double-replies.
